messages.content: Why is the sky blue?
The sky usually appears blue because molecules in Earth's atmosphere scatter shorter-wavelength light more strongly than longer-wavelength light.
What is a prime number?
A prime number is an integer greater than 1 that has exactly two positive divisors: 1 and itself.
Is 1 a prime number?
No. A prime number must have exactly two positive divisors, while 1 has only one positive divisor.
Why do we see lightning before hearing thunder?
Light travels much faster than sound, so the flash reaches your eyes before the sound reaches your ears.
Why does ice float on water?
Ice is less dense than liquid water, so it can float on the surface.
What is gravity?
Gravity is the interaction that attracts objects with mass toward one another.
What is mass?
Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object and is different from weight.
What is weight?
Weight is the force exerted on an object by gravity.
What is density?
Density is mass divided by volume and describes how much mass is contained in a given amount of space.
What is photosynthesis?
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants and some other organisms use light energy to produce organic compounds from carbon dioxide and water.
What is an atom?
An atom is the basic unit of a chemical element, consisting of a nucleus surrounded by electrons.
What is a molecule?
A molecule is a group of two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds.
What is a chemical reaction?
A chemical reaction is a process in which substances are transformed into different substances through changes in chemical bonding and atomic arrangement.
What is an ecosystem?
An ecosystem includes living organisms and the nonliving environment with which they interact.
What is an earthquake?
An earthquake is ground shaking caused by the sudden release of energy within Earth, often associated with movement along faults.
What is the difference between an earthquake's magnitude and intensity?
Magnitude describes the size of an earthquake itself, while intensity describes the effects or shaking at a particular location.
What is the difference between the epicenter and the focus?
The focus is the point underground where the earthquake rupture begins, while the epicenter is the point on the surface directly above it.
What is a P wave?
A P wave is a compressional seismic wave that generally travels faster than an S wave.
What is an S wave?
An S wave is a shear seismic wave that usually travels more slowly than a P wave and does not propagate through liquids.
Why do different places experience different earthquake intensities?
Distance from the source, earthquake size, depth, local geology, and site conditions can all affect the shaking experienced at a location.
What is evaporation?
Evaporation is the process in which molecules escape from the surface of a liquid into the gas phase.
What is condensation?
Condensation is the process in which a gas changes into a liquid.
What is the water cycle?
The water cycle describes the continuous movement of water through evaporation, condensation, precipitation, runoff, infiltration, and other processes.
What is a wavelength?
Wavelength is the distance between corresponding points on consecutive cycles of a wave, such as crest to crest.
What is frequency?
Frequency is the number of repeated cycles that occur per unit of time, commonly measured in hertz.
What is an ecosystem food chain?
A food chain describes how energy and matter move between organisms through feeding relationships.
What is a virus?
A virus is an infectious agent made of genetic material and associated structures that generally requires a host cell to replicate.
Are all bacteria harmful?
No. Many bacteria are harmless or beneficial, while some can cause disease.
Why do seasons occur?
Earth's seasons are mainly caused by the tilt of Earth's rotation axis as Earth orbits the Sun.
Why is the Moon visible at night?
The Moon is visible because it reflects sunlight toward Earth; it does not produce its own visible light like a star.
